podcast.title: $500,000 Deal with Electric Records
podcast.body: His manager, Jerry Brandt, secured a deal with Electric Records for $500,000, which was an enormous sum of money at the time, underscoring the label's significant investment and belief in his potential. "That didn't stop a manager by the name of Jerry Brandt from striking a deal with the electric records for $500,000, a huge amount of money at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: AIDS Diagnosis and Death (1980s)
podcast.body: By the early 1980s, Gerbrieth's "bathhouse habits" led him to contract AIDS. He tragically died on August 3, 1987, notably just one week after his restrictive 10-year contract with Jerry Brandt expired. "By the early 80s, his bathhouse habits had caught up with him and Gerbrieth contracted AIDS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Ambitious Stage Production for Paris Opera House
podcast.body: An additional $200,000 was allocated for a lavish stage production intended to open at the Paris Opera House. This production included elaborate props, such as a 40-foot model of the Empire State Building, which was designed to represent a phallic symbol. "Another $200,000 was spent on a stage production that was supposed to open at the Paris Opera House."

podcast.title: Background as Part-time Drug Addict and Rent Boy
podcast.body: Before his major record deal, Gerbrieth had a background that included being a part-time drug addict and an occasional rent boy. This detail highlights the unconventional and challenging circumstances of his early life. "He was also a part-time drug addict and occasional rent boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Career Collapse and Contractual Issues
podcast.body: His career ultimately collapsed; the Paris shows never happened, and after two albums, Gerbrieth disappeared. He struggled to make music due to an "iron clad 10-year contract" with Jerry Brandt, with whom he was no longer communicating. "The Paris shows never happened and after two albums, Gerbrieth disappeared."

srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: First Openly and Genuinely Gay Rock Star
podcast.body: Gerbrieth (real name Bruce Campbell) is identified as the first rock singer to admit being 100% gay from the outset, making him the world's first openly and genuinely gay rock star. He was also the first gay singer to be signed to a major record label, Electric Records. "Gerbrieth, the world's first openly gay and genuinely gay rock star."

podcast.title: Gerbrieth AD Documentary
podcast.body: A documentary titled "Gerbrieth AD" provides further insight into his life and career, serving as a recommended resource for those interested in learning more about him. "there's a great documentary called Gerbrieth AD. How do you recommend it?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Self-Reference as "True Fairy"
podcast.body: In interviews, Gerbrieth candidly referred to himself using the term "true fairy," openly embracing his identity at a time when such declarations were unprecedented in mainstream rock. "And in interviews, Gerbrieth referred to himself as a true fairy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Whitewashed from Rock History and Posthumous Recognition
podcast.body: For a long time, Gerbrieth's existence was "basically whitewashed from rock history." It is only recently, thanks to a dedicated group of fans (including Morrissey) who discovered him after his death, that he is beginning to receive acknowledgment for his significant contributions to music. "for a long, long time, his existence was basically whitewashed from rock history."

xref.title: Forgotten California Band
xref.body: Pigeon was a California band that has largely been forgotten in rock history. Gerbrieth, then known as Bruce Campbell, was a member of this group before launching his solo career. "He was a member of a forgotten California band called Pigeon."
